plan.choice_policy: Slots coded XXXX XXXX or XXXX XXXX are catalog choice slots. Select courses from the catalog's General Education Core Curriculum (Area I, II, III, IV) or as noted; see program advisor for guided elective options and specialization course selection.
plan.credits_policy: Credit Hours Required for Graduation: 60-63. The Office Management specialization pathway below totals 63 credits (General Core 15 + Occupational 36 + Office Management Specialization 12).
plan.department: School of Business, Cyber, and Design
notes: Source: Augusta Technical College 2026-2027 Academic Catalog, Business Technology AAS (Office Management Specialization). Offered at the Augusta Campus and fully online. Entrance: Fall and Spring. Length: Five Terms.

Specialization slots ('ONE SPECIALIZATION COURSE', 'COMPLETE REMAINING SPECIALIZATION COURSES') are seeded as generic choice slots with the catalog's own wording (3+3+6 = 12 credits of the Office Management Specialization: BUSN 2130, BUSN 2140, BUSN 2290, MGMT 1100); the student chooses with an advisor, per the catalog. The catalog requires advisor consultation before choosing a specialization.

Credit reconciliation: outline items sum to 63 (General Core 15 + Occupational 36 + Office Management Specialization 12); guided pathway sums to 63; both fall within the catalog's 60-63 graduation range. No discrepancy.

The Human Resources Specialization (9 credits) and Project Management Specialization (9 credits) are listed in the catalog outline with NO courses published (empty sections); they cannot be seeded and are not part of this plan.

COLL 1060: students who have earned at least 15 semester hours through an earned credential, transfer credit, or dual enrollment do not need to take COLL 1060; they meet with their advisor to select an advisor-approved elective to replace it.
A grade of 'C' or higher is required for all courses (per catalog program note).
Course-level prerequisites live in the catalog course descriptions and are not individually transcribed here.

Program description: prepares graduates for employment in technology-driven workplaces; word processing, spreadsheet, presentation, and database applications; accounting fundamentals, electronic communications, office management and executive assistant qualification. Optional credentialing: (CMAA) Certified Medical Administrative Assistant, NHA.
plan.transfer_notes: AAS workforce program; no Texas TCCNS equivalencies published. tccns fields mirror the local TCSG course codes for reference only.
